picked.t: Vietnam seeks broader visa exemptions for high-potential tourism markets
picked.body: Under a draft resolution that the government submitted to the National Assembly on Saturday, visa policies will also be designed with flexibility tailored to specific markets, with priority given to high-spending, long-stay tourists, repeat travelers and those combining leisure trips with business, conferences or seminars. The draft covers seven key policy groups, including investment incentives, business support, nighttime economy development, human resource, visa policies and tourism infrastructure. Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism Lam Thi Phuong Thanh said the proposed policies aim to remove existing bottlenecks and attract investment, positioning tourism as a key economic sector and a driver of the country's goal of achieving double-digit economic growth. The National Assembly is expected to vote on adopting the resolution on Nov. 21. Vietnam received 19.5 million international visitors in the first 10 months of 2026, a 13.8% increase from a year earlier, as it eyes 25 million foreign arrivals by the end of this year. China, South Korea and Russia are the country's biggest source of inbound tourists. Vietnam currently grants visa exemptions to citizens of 39 countries, allowing stays from 14 to 90 days.

picked.t: 하노이서 제1회 한-베트남 AI·반도체 콘퍼런스 12~13일 개최…VKAISS 2026
picked.body: 한국과 베트남의 인공지능(AI)·반도체 협력을 논의하는 첫 콘퍼런스 '2026 베트남-한국 AI·반도체 서밋'이 오는 12~13일 하노이에서 개최된다. 이번 행사에는 양국 400여 명의 참석자와 함께 50여 개 반도체 기업과 연구기관, 대학 등 현지 관계자들이 참석할 것으로 전망된다. 롯데호텔이 운영하는 L7웨스트레이크하노이바이롯데(L7 WEST LAKE HANOI BY LOTTE)에서 열릴 이번 콘퍼런스는 베트남 과학기술부가 후원하고, AI·디지털기술국과 FPT그룹, 한국팹리스산업협회, 베트남소프트웨어·IT서비스협회(VINASA) 반도체산업발전위원회가 공동 주최한다. 주최 측에 따르면, 'VKAISS 2026'로 명명된 이번 행사는 ‘ONE VISION – NEW HORIZONS’이라는 슬로건 아래 양국의 AI·반도체 협력 증진을 위해 기획된 것으로, 베트남 기업들이 △회로 설계 △패키징 △칩 테스트 △AI 응용 분야에서 한국 파트너를 찾는 좋은 기회가 될 것으로 기대를 모은다. 이번 행사는 지난해 또 럼(To Lam) 베트남 공산당 서기장 겸 국가주석의 한국 국빈 방문과 지난 4월 이재명 대통령의 베트남 국빈 방문 당시 양국이 합의한 협력, 특히 AI와 반도체 분야에서 협력 강화 합의 이행에 기여하는 것을 목표로 한다. 이에 따라 행사는 베트남과 한국 간 인력 개발과 AI·반도체 협력 정책을 주제로 두 차례의 토론회가 진행될 예정이며, 이 외 양국 기업이 투자 파트너와 기술 이전, 공동 교육 협력을 찾을 기회를 마련할 수 있도록 비즈니스매칭과 기술 전시회도 열릴 예정이다. 또한 행사에는 양국 관련 기업 외 현지 반도체 연구소와 대학, 베트남 과학기술 분야 관련 부처 및 기관, 단체장, 주베트남 한국대사관 관계자들이 참석할 예정으로, 이 외 양국 주요 반도체 및 기술 관련 협회, 가천대·FPT대·하노이과기대·우정통신대 등 교육기관, 그리고 박닌시·성남시 등 양국 지방정부 관계자들이 참석할 예정이다. 주최 측은 “이번 행사가 반도체 관련 정책과 기술, 투자, 인력 양성을 잇는 가교 역할을 하여 양국 반도체 협력을 촉진하고 구체적인 성과를 창출하기를 기대한다”고 밝혔다.

picked.t: American-style dining in Ho Chi Minh City skyscraper
picked.body: Opened in late September, the restaurant is the first Asian location for the American steakhouse chain founded in 1990. Spanning around 500 m2 and with 120 covers, the restaurant operates as an authentic American steakhouse. Stanley Ko, president of Ko Hospitality Group, the operator of The Capital Grille in Vietnam, says Ho Chi Minh City was selected as the brand's first regional destination due to its dynamic economy, sizable business community, and diners who are open to western foods. The restaurant serves an à la carte menu featuring appetizers, soups, salads, beef, seafood, side dishes, and desserts, with portion sizes adjusted to suit local dining habits. Beef takes center stage with diverse options in cuts, portion weights, levels of doneness, and sauces. The eatery exclusively serves imported USDA Prime beef, the highest grade in the U.S. Department of Agriculture quality system, known for abundant marbling that enhances tenderness and flavor when cooked. The restaurant's signature offering is its dry-aged beef (pictured). Aged for 18 to 24 days in a temperature- and humidity-controlled room, the process reduces moisture content, tenderizes muscle fibers, and deepens the natural flavor profile. A 680-gram dry-aged steak portion, good for three to four diners, costs VND3.2 million (US$124). The menu also highlights recognizable American classics. The caviar dip, priced at VND1.9 million, offers a twist on standard "chips and dip" by pairing crispy potato chips with caviar and caramelized onion dip. The lobster bisque, priced at VND450,000 per portion, is a steakhouse staple rooted in French tradition. It features a velvety crustacean-based broth combined with cream and seasonings, served alongside Spanish sherry, an aged fortified wine that elevates the soup's aroma and depth of flavor. Meanwhile, the lobster mac and cheese, priced at VND800,000, features macaroni tossed in cheese sauce and mixed with lobster meat. This is a variation of "mac and cheese," an iconic dish introduced to formal American banquets by President Thomas Jefferson in the early 19th century before becoming a household staple following Kraft's boxed release in 1937. Shannon Dean and Michael Zack, tourists from the U.S. visiting HCMC in late October, dined at the restaurant to enjoy some familiar flavors after trying local dishes. Having visited The Capital Grille in Las Vegas before, both said the food and decor closely matched U.S. standards, creating a sense of familiarity. For them, the highlight was pairing a familiar meal with panoramic city views at prices similar to the brand's U.S. locations. Local diners have also shared their impressions. A family of four from Ho Chi Minh City visited the restaurant to experience high-floor dining in the city center. Ordering a 10-course meal across appetizers, soups, steaks, seafood, and desserts, they observed that the dishes featured large portions, rich and creamy flavors, and fewer green vegetable options, with some items feeling slightly dry for Vietnamese palates. Their meal cost nearly VND13 million, which was similar to prices at other high-end steakhouses in the city. A staff member sets the table before welcoming dinner guests to the restaurant, which charges a 5% service charge. The restaurant is open from 11:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. and from 5:30 p.m. to 9:30 p.m. Guests are required to make reservations in advance and can use a dedicated elevator and private entrance (pictured).

picked.t: Vietnam eyes 24/7 entertainment zones, tax holidays for billion-dollar tourism projects
picked.body: The draft resolution on special mechanisms and policies for tourism development, submitted to lawmakers on Saturday, sets out seven groups of policies, ranging from investment incentives and business support to the night-time economy, workforce training and infrastructure. Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism Lam Thi Phuong Thanh said the policies aim to clear bottlenecks, draw investment and make tourism a key economic sector that helps drive the country's double-digit growth target. Under the draft, incentives would be tiered by investment capital, number of jobs and type of project, and concentrated in Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City and Da Nang as well as tourism centers, national tourism areas and areas with national tourism potential. High-quality tourism projects with total investment of at least VND3 trillion, at least VND1.5 trillion of it for tourism components, and creating at least 1,000 jobs could receive infrastructure support inside and outside the project site and priority in promotion. Domestic investors in this tier could also rent unused state-owned houses and land. Catalyst tourism projects worth at least VND10 trillion, with at least VND5 trillion for tourism components and at least 1,500 jobs, would be eligible on a five-year pilot basis for a preferential corporate income tax rate as low as 10%, half Vietnam's standard 20% rate, plus land rent exemptions or reductions set by the government. The highest incentives would go to strategic projects with total investment of at least VND30 trillion, including at least VND15 trillion for tourism components, and at least 2,000 jobs. They could operate for up to 70 years, be exempt from corporate income tax for up to four years and have their tax cut by up to 50% for no more than nine years after that. None of the three tiers would cover casino, prize-winning electronic gaming, betting or real estate components, Thanh said, as incentives would apply only to tourism activities. The government also proposed a pilot cut of up to 30% in land rent for landscaped areas, green space, water surfaces and shared spaces not used directly for business at resort hotels rated four stars or above, provided they are in tourism centers or national tourism areas and have a gross building density below 25%. Businesses opening new air routes for tourism could receive support, as could travel firms and accommodation providers that sign long-term contracts to buy products certified under the One Commune One Product (OCOP) program, which promotes local specialties. For new business models, the draft offers incentives for complexes combining tourism, entertainment, culture and sports; for tourism combined with healthcare and medical treatment; and for activities involving local communities. Businesses would also be encouraged to use artificial intelligence, virtual reality, augmented reality and other new technologies to develop products and improve the visitor experience. Some large-scale performing arts complexes, concert halls, festival streets, integrated entertainment zones and night-time economy activities would be allowed to operate 24/7 under a pilot of up to five years. They could follow shortened administrative procedures and obtain a one-time license for large international art programs and events held regularly, instead of reapplying for each edition. The state budget would fund training for high-quality tourism workers in management, foreign languages, vocational skills, digital transformation, digital content creation and innovation, as well as for local workers in community tourism areas. Budget funding would be prioritized for essential infrastructure and multimodal transport links from international gateways to growth poles, key tourism centers and national tourism areas. The state would also support the national tourism promotion program and help localities develop distinctive products and community tourism in ethnic minority, mountainous, border, island and disadvantaged areas. Reviewing the draft, Nguyen Dac Vinh, chairman of the National Assembly's Committee for Culture and Society, said the committee supported special policies focused on projects able to lead and spread tourism growth in key areas. But the committee found the incentives for strategic catalyst projects had been set at a very high level without an assessment of the benefits they would bring, and asked that they be weighed carefully. It also asked the government to explain how the minimum capital thresholds and the share of capital reserved for tourism were set, and whether the criteria for classifying projects were feasible. The committee said casino, prize-winning electronic gaming, betting and real estate components must stay outside the incentives, and that support should be tied to project results so the policy cannot be used to develop businesses outside priority sectors.
